name: How much does a multifamily renovation cost per unit in Los Angeles in 2026?

mainEntity.name: What is the realistic per-unit budget range for a multifamily renovation in Los Angeles right now?
mainEntity.text: What is the realistic per-unit budget range for a multifamily renovation in Los Angeles right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: A realistic Los Angeles budget depends on whether the work is cosmetic, a value-add refresh, or a full gut renovation. Light upgrades such as paint, flooring, fixtures, and cabinet resurfacing are the lowest-cost tier. Kitchens, bathrooms, in-unit laundry, rewiring, and plumbing changes move the project into a much higher range. In LA, owners also need to account for permit costs, design fees, inspection delays, material escalation, and contingency. For occupied buildings, phased work and tenant coordination can add indirect cost. A good budget should separate hard costs from soft costs and include a contingency reserve. If a quote looks unusually low, it often excludes permit complexity, hidden conditions, or tenant-related logistics.
acceptedAnswer.description: Per-unit multifamily renovation costs in Los Angeles vary widely by scope, but light cosmetic updates can start around $10,000 to $20,000 per unit, while full renovations often range from $30,000 to $80,000 per unit or more. Down-to-studs work, utility upgrades, and luxury finishes can push costs much higher.
